sn37.3:1.1: _Mātugāma_ literally means “motherkind” (cf. the archaic “motherkin”). It is a word for women in Pali, but a problematic one. It does not seem to be in use outside of Buddhist texts, and perhaps was coined by the Buddha. Throughout the Pātimokkha it is used in apposition with _bhikkhu_, whereas _itthī_ (“woman”_) is used with _purisa_ (“man”). But there is no corresponding male form, so _bhikkhunī_ just takes _purisa_. However, this does not obtain in the Suttas, as we see here _mātugāma_ used with _purisa_. Grammatically it is always singular, but it is used in both singular and plural senses. We cvan see this in this Sutta: in this sentence, it must be “womankind” in general since it is paired with “men” in plural, whereas below it is paired with “man” so must be “woman”. The commentary says it is any human woman, even one born that very day. I reluctantly use “female” to distinguish it, but I confess I am unsure what the connotation of this word is.
